investigate-complete-registry-identities.text: As a registry integrator, I want to inspect candidate identities, distinguish unsafe readings and replay their examples before adopting a new law.

story-and-status.text: This isolated Lean project investigates #741 at the supported root compiler. It requires the unchanged root model from ../... Every candidate declaration is a hypothesis; no accepted model, application, corpus, coverage record or release behavior changes. Approvals follow the operator's recorded complete-identity ruling in specs/741-no-pin-model/decisions.md. All public statements have sorry bodies. The compiled ledger marks them STATED, with separate markers for rejected or potentially false readings. The kernel reports sorryAx alongside standard axioms; none is a proved guarantee. Witnesses and mutant falsifications are separate kernel-checked concrete instances with no proof holes. Their predicates are checked for definitional equality against the statement signatures; they never import the unproved statements. The name-only safety claim is a rejected reading expected to be refutable. One evaluated fixture reuses an approval under a different state policy with the same state name. Policy-only recognition is also expected refutable: a genuine witness carrying a fabricated state datum satisfies that reading. The authenticated reading refuses that fixture under its explicit name/provenance checks. These evaluations are not general proofs, transaction execution or acceptance of either recognition rule.

identity-and-evidence-boundaries.text: Derivation is acyclic: release determines application policy, then state policy. The seed independently determines state name. Complete policy/name registry identity then enters approval and role naming. Hash and Codec are explicit pure parameters; the tagged natural-number encoding and finite lookup hash are not Cardano serialization or cryptographic implementations. Encoding and hash separation are distinct finite-domain premises. No unconditional injectivity theorem is asserted. State, witness, trie-ready and application tags have explicit roles under the hypothetical shared policy. Request-tag separation here uses only registry, role and key. It does not cover the economic request payload or per-request nonce. Approval payloads retain edge, key, owner, destination and nonce. No economic admission, custody or supply claim follows from this identity projection. Observation.provenance is supplied authenticated-origin evidence. This project does not establish its truth from a datum, token location or transaction history. Without the stated finite separation premises, names can collide. The recognition question remains open. TxView records spent references, output assets, mint per complete asset and invoked policies. It has no ledger validity judgement, script evaluator or UTxO update. A single transaction may spend a seed once and invoke two application-specific state policies, yielding the same seed name under different policies. A list of observations satisfying historyAllows instead carries a separate spent-once premise. Binding either observation to an accepted ledger/history is still owed to #679/#680. Neither implies global uniqueness of a name across policies.

reproduce-the-evidence.text: Run nix develop --quiet -c just no-pin-identity from the repository root. The Development shell checks job runs this same recipe. It builds the isolated library and generic oracle, elaborates the fresh environment report, checks compiled statement identities and axioms against statements.json, and replays corpus.json through the oracle. Successful local execution is not hosted CI evidence. Report.lean discovers public cases, guards and roles from compiled constructors. It executes each case and measures which selectors change it; inversion rows must cover exactly that discovered extent. Every statement row needs an executed antecedent witness and at least one owned selector with a positive candidate instance and a false mutant instance. Normalizing that selector to none must give the identical compiled proposition as the positive control. The mutation selector exists only for the mutant ledger. All statements are stated at Mutation.none. A selector flips one atomic guard in the same candidate definition; the report executes its truth table at every discovered site and refuses multi-guard changes. The guards include every condition in approval, recognition and genesis, plus history uniqueness. Inversions state the full acceptance equivalence, so a mutant that wrongly refuses a valid input is detected too. The oracle at .lake/build/bin/no-pin-oracle reads JSON Scenario lines and returns Boolean results. Each scenario supplies a named Query surface and a mutation selector. It contains no theorem-specific expected-result code. Malformed JSON or scenario fields exit nonzero. The corpus is a computed replay of public definition cases and their guard flips, not a ledger-accepted lifecycle or a replacement for the separate Lean theorem fixtures.

limits-and-next-decision.text: No general statement is proved or constructively refuted in this stage. No simulator, validator, builder, reader, custody reconciliation, economic configuration migration or compatibility policy is accepted. The termination-custody ruling belongs to its later stage. Independent statement review and the operator's remaining decisions precede proof work or any accepted-law change.
